data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1919 experienced an overall run-off deterioration of GBP 12.5 million in 2014, primarily driven by adverse claims development in the Accident & Health class, particularly from the 2013 underwriting year due to increased exposure and poor attritional loss experience. This was partially offset by favorable claims development and reserve releases in the Casualty and Financial classes due to better than expected claims experience. The Energy class was impacted by a significant large loss in the Onshore account and an adverse decision on a 2010 Specialty Property claim.

increase in exposure in the 2013 underwriting year, with relatively poor associated attritional loss experience
better than expected claims experience across all years resulting in reserve releases

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Specific LOB movements are not quantified, only the overall prior year deterioration and its primary driver (A&H) are quantified. The gross premium mix uses the regulatory segmental analysis which combines direct and reinsurance for some categories, and then has a separate 'Reinsurance' category for the remainder.
